clauses.clause: Explain concepts by interpreting texts.
Learn concepts by interpreting texts.
Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.

verdicts.evidence: Invite students to use the response sheet to capture the things they noticed and wondered about the sun, moon, and stars. Tell them that they can use pictures and words to show what they notice and what they wonder. As students write and draw, circulate to offer support. Prompt students by referencing the mystery sky photos and asking students to articulate what they shared with their partners during the Picture Tea Party protocol or the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol. Remind students that they can draw and write to show what they notice and wonder.
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret texts (story, photos, videos) to learn and explain concepts about the sun, moon, and stars, and construct their own texts (written/drawn responses) to demonstrate understanding.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Explain and learn concepts and processes by interpreting and constructing texts. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Summarize sections of the text to maintain understanding.
Visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding.

verdicts.evidence: After reading and discussing 'Elvin, the Boy Who Loved the Sky,' support comprehension and provide options for expression by inviting three students to each illustrate one of the paragraphs in the story. Display the story with illustrations in an accessible place for students to refer to throughout the unit during subsequent readings.
verdicts.rationale: Students summarize and visualize sections of the text by discussing and illustrating paragraphs, directly supporting both clauses of the standard.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Summarize and visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding. (I)

clauses.clause: Refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion.
clauses.note: During the read-aloud, students answer teacher questions by citing specific details from the story about what Elvin observes and wonders.

clauses.clause: Explore various sources of information, including print, digital, and personal communication.
clauses.note: Students engage with a print read-aloud, examine photos in a small-group protocol, and later view multiple videos and discuss their observations with peers.

verdicts.evidence: Draw students' attention back to the text and read aloud the second paragraph. Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group: 'What does Elvin observe about the sun?' ... 'What does Elvin wonder about the sun?' ... Draw students' attention back to the text and read aloud the third paragraph. Ask: 'What does Elvin observe about the moon?' ... 'What does Elvin wonder about the moon?' ... Draw students' attention back to the text and read the final paragraph. Display a selection of the mystery sky photos and tell students that they are each going to get a chance to look closely at one of the photos that the photographer gave to Elvin.
verdicts.rationale: Students reference specific parts of a read-aloud to answer questions and also explore multiple sources (story, photos, videos) through guided discussion and protocols.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Reference parts of texts to address a specific topic or question and explore various sources of information to make connections across a broad range of topics.

clauses.clause: Establish a purpose and set goals for reading
clauses.note: Teacher sets a clear purpose for listening/reading (focus on Elvin’s questions) and students proceed under that purpose.

clauses.clause: Monitor comprehension and adjust strategies as needed
clauses.note: No explicit monitoring or adjustment of strategies is taught or required of students.

clauses.clause: Scan and skim the text to note useful structures and sections
clauses.note: Students listen to a read-aloud; no skimming/scanning tasks are assigned.

clauses.clause: Draw from and integrate prior knowledge with the text, addressing inconsistencies or gaps
clauses.note: Students are prompted to connect the text to their own experiences (e.g., sharing if they have lain on the grass to look at the sky).

clauses.clause: Summarize and visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding
clauses.note: A few students illustrate paragraphs, but there is no whole-class requirement to summarize or visualize sections.

clauses.clause: Make and track predictions about upcoming events and information
clauses.note: Students predict from the title and later share predictions about images during the Picture Tea Party.

clauses.clause: Make, track, and support inferences about different levels of meaning
clauses.note: Questions focus on literal observations and the character’s wonders; inference-making is not required.

clauses.clause: Determine meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using context, academic vocabulary, and word parts
clauses.note: Vocabulary meanings are provided by the teacher (Word Wall); students do not derive meanings from context or word parts.

verdicts.evidence:
- Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
- 'Based on the title of the story, what do you think this story will be about?' (a little boy who likes things in the sky; a little boy who likes the clouds; a little boy who likes to look at the sky)
- Say:
- 'As I read this story, I want you to think hard about all of the things Elvin wonders about and all of the questions he has.'
verdicts.rationale: Students engage with a read-aloud and visual texts using comprehension strategies such as setting a purpose (prompted) and making predictions, and they connect to prior knowledge. However, they do not practice monitoring/adjusting strategies, skimming/scanning, inference, or deriving word meanings, so only some clauses are met.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text:
Engage with a range of complex texts for a variety of tasks and purposes, accessing and using strategies for comprehension before, during, and after reading as part of the meaning-making process.
Comprehension strategies are tools that students should develop throughout their K-12 education as they work to interpret increasingly complex texts. The effectiveness of these strategies depends largely on the texts themselves, the reasons students engage with them, and the preferences and knowledge bases of individual students. For these reasons, students should receive instruction in a variety of comprehension strategies. Students should learn to select and apply strategies flexibly in order to make sense of the text and accomplish their goals.

clauses.clause: Interpret texts to analyze ideas.
clauses.note: Students view/read texts (story, photos, videos) and share what they notice and wonder, interpreting to discuss ideas about the sun, moon, and stars.

clauses.clause: Construct texts to evaluate ideas.
clauses.note: Students draw/write notices and wonders, but do not evaluate ideas; no task asks them to judge or assess ideas.

verdicts.evidence: Tell students there are a few videos of the sky, sun, moon, and stars to see, and that as they watch the videos they should look carefully to see what they notice about the sky and what they observe about the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky in each of the videos. Tell students they should also think about the questions they have as they watch the videos. ... Guide students through the protocol using the following question and sentence frame: -'What is one thing you noticed about the sun in the video?' -'I noticed that the sun __________.'
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret multimedia texts to discuss observations and questions (analysis), but their writing/drawing records noticing/wondering rather than evaluating ideas; no evaluation task is present.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Interpret and construct texts to aid the analysis and evaluation of texts and ideas. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Identify techniques used to craft expository texts, including main topic and supporting details.
clauses.note: No explicit identification of expository techniques.

clauses.clause: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
clauses.note: No explicit description of connections.

clauses.clause: Use knowledge of expository techniques to introduce a topic, supply facts about the topic, and provide a sense of closure.
clauses.note: No evidence of using expository techniques to create texts.

verdicts.rationale: The lesson does not address expository text structure or techniques, nor do students identify or use them.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Identify and use expository techniques to shape understanding.

clauses.clause: Identify techniques used to craft stories, including characters, setting, major events, and dialogue.
clauses.note: Students focus on observations and questions about celestial objects; they do not identify story elements as narrative techniques.

clauses.clause: Identify a simple plot with a problem and solution.
clauses.note: No task asks students to determine a problem/solution or plot.

clauses.clause: Describe traits of the main characters and explain how their words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
clauses.note: Students briefly note something about Elvin but do not analyze traits or connect to a message/moral.

clauses.clause: With adult support, compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories across diverse cultures.
clauses.note: No comparison across characters, stories, or cultures occurs.

clauses.clause: Use knowledge of narrative techniques to create texts that share real or imagined experiences and events with a sense of closure.
clauses.note: Students write notices and wonders about science topics, not narratives with closure.

verdicts.rationale: The lesson centers on observing and asking questions about the sun, moon, and stars. Students neither analyze narrative elements (characters, setting, plot) nor produce narrative writing.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Identify and use narrative techniques to shape understanding.

clauses.clause: Use texts to build knowledge.
Use texts to develop skills.
Use texts to make informed decisions.
Use texts to share information and ideas.

verdicts.evidence:
Tell students that now that they have shared what they noticed and wondered about the sun, moon, and stars with their classmates, they are going to write down and draw what they notice and wonder.
Direct students' attention to the Noticing and Wondering response sheet, pencils, and crayons already at their workspace.
Invite students to use the response sheet to capture the things they noticed and wondered about the sun, moon, and stars. Tell them that they can use pictures and words to show what they notice and what they wonder.
verdicts.rationale: Students use texts (story, photos, videos) to build knowledge, develop observation/questioning skills, and share information and ideas through discussion and writing/drawing.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Make use of texts to build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, and share information and ideas. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Identify who is speaking at various points in a text.
clauses.note: No evidence of identifying the speaker in the text.

verdicts.rationale: The lesson does not address identifying the speaker or narrator in the text.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Investigate the relationships between authors and speakers in texts.

clauses.clause: Ask questions about topics of interest for research.
Conduct research individually or collaboratively by gathering and organizing information from multiple sources using graphic organizers or support aids.
clauses.note: No research using multiple sources.

clauses.clause: Share relevant and accurate information through different communication modes.
clauses.note: No research-based sharing; only observations/questions.

verdicts.rationale: Students ask questions, but do not conduct research using multiple sources or share research-based information as required by the standard.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Build knowledge about the world by asking or generating questions about topics of interest, researching the answers, using multiple sources, and communicating relevant and accurate information about the topic.
